q: Customers with the same features now churn more often than before, because a competitor launched a cheaper offer. What kind of change is this?
e: The relationship between inputs and outcome, P(y | X), has changed. It needs labels to detect and calls for retraining.

q: Which test fits a categorical column such as `contract`?
e: Chi-square compares category frequencies. KS and Wasserstein need ordered numeric values.

q: The PSI of `support_calls_90d` between the training baseline and this week is 0.27. How is that usually read?
o: A significant shift that deserves investigation
e: A common rule of thumb: below 0.1 small, 0.1 to 0.2 moderate, 0.2 or more significant. PSI measures the size of the shift, not accuracy.

q: You monitor a table of model requests with features, predictions and later labels. Which profile type gives model quality metrics per window?
o: Any profile type, because labels are optional
e: An InferenceLog profile knows the prediction, label and model id columns, so it computes accuracy, F1 or ROC AUC per window and model version.

q: A KS test on 50 million rows gives a p-value of 1e-12, but the mean moved from 3.01 to 3.02. What should you conclude?
o: With huge samples tiny shifts are significant; check the size of the shift before acting
KS tests cannot be used on large data
e: Significance grows with sample size. Use effect-size metrics such as PSI or Wasserstein distance and business thresholds to decide.
